# SOP-P3-L3-02 Product changeover - Machining line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled procedure for product changeover on the Machining line to ensure consistent setup, safe operations, and traceable records. This procedure addresses mechanical adjustments, hydraulic press maintenance checks, and lubricant verification required to bring the line from run-state to next product configuration.

Background and rationale
2. Changeovers are a primary source of variation and unplanned downtime. Standardizing steps reduces scrap, protects tooling and press components, and ensures operator safety. Sequence is structured to isolate energy, validate tooling, and verify lubrication and bolting critical to press integrity. Where press bolt preload is required, the specified torque must be applied and recorded to maintain press safety and alignment.

Preconditions (must be satisfied before beginning)
3. Line is in a completed production state and halted under controlled stop. Utility and lockout procedures are available from SB-1005 and SB-1010. Operators must have reviewed SOP-P3-L3-04 for material staging rules. All affected equipment present: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Required parts and tooling staged and matched to the next product.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE during changeover: safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection for near-press operations, and face shield when removing guards. Respiratory protection is not required unless specified by task-level hazard assessment.

Tools and consumables
5. Only use calibrated torque tools for fastener verification. Use the lubricant with specified part number for press lubrication. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-340.

Changeover steps (numbered sequence)
6. Step 1 — Prepare and communicate
   - Notify line lead and maintenance that changeover will begin. Post lockout tagout schedule per SB-1005. Confirm tooling list matches next product.

7. Step 2 — Isolate energy sources
   - Execute lockout/tagout on electrical supply and hydraulic isolation per SB-1005 and SB-1010. Verify stored energy is bled and locked. Confirm isolation at EQ-P3-L3-HP03 before any press work.

8. Step 3 — Remove product-specific fixtures
   - Remove and inspect fixtures and soft jaws from EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Clean locating surfaces. Tag and store fixtures in assigned bins for the next run.

9. Step 4 — Inspect press components
   - With energy isolated, inspect EQ-P3-L3-HP03 ram, platen faces, and fasteners for wear, cracks, or foreign material. Replace or escalate any discrepancy through maintenance per SB-1010.

10. Step 5 — Verify and set main ram bolt torque
    - Using a calibrated torque wrench, verify the main ram bolt torque at EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Apply the specified torque and record. The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m.
    - Rationale: Correct bolt preload maintains ram alignment and prevents fretting and accelerated wear. Example: if bolt shows evidence of loosening, re-torque to the specified value and escalate for root-cause evaluation.

11. Step 6 — Lubrication
    - Confirm lubricant supply and fill points on EQ-P3-L3-HP03. Use lubricant with the specified part number. The lubricant part number for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is CFW-LUB-340.
    - Rationale: Using the specified lubricant ensures proper viscosity and additive package for high-load press components. Record batch or lot identifier for traceability.

12. Step 7 — Install new tooling and perform alignment
    - Mount new tooling to EQ-P3-L3-SB01 and EQ-P3-L3-CN02. Use alignment gauges or mating references. Check for interference and clamp according to tooling manufacturer guidance.

13. Step 8 — Functional checks under low energy
    - Remove locks on control circuits only to permit single-cycle runs at reduced energy per SB-1010. Cycle press with verified guards in place to confirm motion and clearances. Observe hydraulic pressures and motion smoothness; any abnormal noise or drift requires re-isolation.

14. Step 9 — Trial production and inspection
    - Produce trial parts and inspect per product acceptance criteria. Record dimensional checks and any rework. If trial parts pass, proceed to full run following production release protocol.

15. Step 10 — Clean up and return to service
    - Remove tools not required for full production, restore guards, and return all lockout devices. Notify line lead and update production board.

Examples and decision guidance
16. Example: If during Step 5 retorque, bolt turns without achieving specified torque, mark as unacceptable and escalate to maintenance. Example: If lubricant batch tag is missing, quarantine supply and source replacement labeled CFW-LUB-340 before proceeding.

Records to keep
17. Maintain the following records in the changeover log:
   - Operator name and signature.
   - Maintenance technician name and signature for torque and lubrication verification.
   - Record of torque application and tool calibration reference.
   - Lubricant part number and batch/lot identifier.
   - Trial part inspection results and disposition.
   - Any nonconformances and corrective actions.
   Store records per document control retention rules and reference SB-1005 for storage location.

Nonconformance and escalation
18. If any step cannot be completed to standard, stop the changeover and escalate to maintenance and production supervision. Use SB-1010 for mechanical repair workflow.

Training and competency
19. Only personnel trained on these procedures and on the specific equipment EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03 may perform changeovers. Training records should be maintained against operator personnel files.

References
20. See SB-1005, SB-1010, SOP-P3-L3-04 for related lockout, maintenance, and material staging procedures.

Sign-off
21. Operator signature: ______________________ Date: ______________________  
22. Maintenance signature (torque/lubrication verification): ______________________ Date: ______________________  
23. Production lead sign-off: ______________________ Date: ______________________

Revision history
24. Rev E current.
